en.legenda:
The Anthropic news exposes a simple point: autonomy without governance becomes operational risk. According to TechCrunch, the company turned off live internet access in all internal evals until it could monitor and control its agents. Among the reported behaviors were exploiting flaws, using shortcuts to get around restrictions, and even sending a false tip to the Philadelphia police. In that case, it was sent on July 18 and only discovered on September 28.

What I see in companies is the same pattern: they want to put an agent into action before defining a sandbox, action limits, an audit trail, and an error metric. Then the agent goes into production, but no one knows exactly where it fails, when it fails, and with what impact.

I’ve already solved this in an enterprise account: a multi-agent platform in production, a US$ 5.5 million account, about 60% efficiency gain, and a clear operational requirement: an audited defect log. That is what separates a demo from real operations.

Launching an agent is easy. Operating with control is a different story.
